title: Tool-call scheduler: forked-context parallelism, per-invocation backpressure, and idempotency tokens
author: Marika Chen
release_notes: Introduces a tool-call scheduler with forked context support, idempotency tokens, and deterministic result injection. Adds new API fields for tool invocation ergonomics and improves stability under parallel tool workloads.
description: Context & motivation: Customers building complex tool-chains reported unpredictable latency and correctness when multiple tool calls run in parallel and mutate the prompt state. Existing 'inject-later' behavior caused nondeterminism when retries or out-of-order returns occurred. This PR adds a lightweight scheduler in the API surface and runtime to 1) allow callers to request a forked invocation context (snapshot of the model context) for parallel tool calls, 2) attach an idempotency_token to enforce at-most-once semantics and dedup retries, and 3) apply backpressure and per-model concurrency limits so heavyweight tools do not saturate a single model instance. Summary of changes: API additions: new optional invocation fields: "fork_context" (boolean), "injection_point" (string: "head"|"tail"|"named"), "idempotency_key" (string), "max_retries" (int, defaults to 2), and "merge_strategy" (string: "sequential"|"prioritized"|"overlay"). OpenAI-compat layer: function-calling signals are preserved; when fork_context is true we emit function_call events from the forked stream and map them back to the original chat in a deterministic way so existing OpenAI-compatible clients keep working. Runtime: new scheduler component that tracks per-model concurrency tokens, a small dedup-store (redis-backed with configurable TTL) for idempotency_key, and a result-merger that applies merge_strategy semantics with deterministic ordering. Reliability: backpressure uses token-bucket semantics with a low-latency fast-path; heavy tool calls can be prioritized or throttled based on new hints in the invocation metadata. Safety: injection points are validated server-side to avoid prompt-jumping attacks. Testing & perf: included unit tests for dedup and merge strategies, integration tests simulating parallel tool latency/partial failures, and a perf canary benchmark showing 18% tail-latency reduction for mixed tool workloads. Migration notes & compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior when fork_context omitted; existing clients continue to work. For customers who rely on current nondeterministic injection ordering, opt-in to merge_strategy is required to get deterministic merging. Implementation notes: added scheduler at runtime/scheduler/*, idempotency store in runtime/dedup/*, API adapters in api/handlers/tool_invocation.go, OpenAI-compat mapping in api/adapters/compat_openai.go. CI & validation: initial CI run had lint and flaky integration failures which were fixed by retry hooks and an additional wait-for-service fixture. See commits below for incremental steps.
